newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says develops world's first 4-gigabit DRAM.
newsitem.headline: NEC says develops world's first 4-gigabit DRAM.

text.p: Japanese electronics firm NEC Corp announced on Thursday that it had developed the world's first four-gigabit dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chip, the most sophisticated memory chip yet.
NEC said its technology had been confirmed by the global semiconductor body, the International Solid State Circuits Conference in the United Sates.
A four-gigabit DRAM is capable of storing data equivalent to 16,000 newspaper pages, NEC said. A gigabit is one billion bits. DRAM chips are used mainly in personal computers.
NEC, the world's second-largest memory chip maker after South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co, said it had beaten its Japanese, South Korean and American rivals in developing the chip.

"NEC is the first in the world to have developed a four-gigabit DRAM chip. We aim to send out sample shipments by 2000 and seek an early launch of the product," NEC vice president Hajime Sasaki told a news conference.
NEC and Japan's Hitachi Ltd developed one-gigabit DRAMs at almost the same time in 1995, an NEC spokesman said.

Commercial production of the four-gigabit chips will not begin until after the turn of the century, however, as the current mainstay chip is still the 16-megabit DRAM chip, which although relatively much less sophisticated can store the equivalent of up to 128 newspaper pages of information.
Demand for the next-generation 64-megabit DRAM chip is expected to peak in late 1998.
Samsung Electronics is part of the Samsung Group.
